newsitem.title: USA: Fannie Mae okayed for mortgage insurance.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae okayed for mortgage insurance.

text.p: Fannie Mae received authorization last week to begin offering a controversial mortgage insurance program, but a top lawmaker urged the company not to go forward with the plan.

In a letter dated June 23 and obtained by Reuters on Monday, U.S. Secretary of Housing and Urban Development Andrew Cuomo determined that Fannie Mae could offer its "Mortgage Protection Plan," despite the misgivings of some lawmakers.

Under the program, Fannie Mae would purchase insurance policies to cover mortgage payments for first-time homebuyers who become unemployed or disabled during the first five years of their loans. Such a policy would pay off the entire mortgage if the borrower died.

House Banking Committee chairman Jim Leach asked Cuomo to review the legality of the insurance plan in April. The Iowa Republican asserted that the plan amounted to unfair competition for insurance companies.
On Monday, Leach called HUD's verdict "a close call, narrowly based, legalistic decision."

"A government-sponsored enterprise, such as Fannie Mae, should not expand out of its traditional role of providing money for the secondary housing market into an area already well served by private industry," Leach said.

Because Fannie Mae has the implicit backing of the federal government, it borrows at lower rates than private insurance companies, Leach noted. "Fannie Mae's advantaged funding costs will make MPP a more profitable venture for it than it would for fully private companies," Leach said.
Fannie Mae officials were not immediately available for comment.
Cuomo said in his letter that the program met the standards for permissible Fannie Mae activities as set out in the Federal Housing Enterprises Financial Safety and Soundness Act of 1992.
